why: Definitions agree: the project's tangentSpace E C O x₁ is B's TxOB R x₁ = {h | (x₁,h) ∈ {(r x, Dr(x)h)}} = range Dr(x₁) for every retraction R onto O (TOB R = R.tangent, retractTangent_eq); the fields of TangentPre are exactly B's IsTupleB (levelSetB = levelSet). The two relations point in opposite directions: project Rel p q is T(ψ∘φ⁻¹)(φ(x),h) = (ψ(x),h') (p's vector moved to q's chart, both components); B's RelB p q is the text's D(φ∘ψ⁻¹∘r)(ψ(x))h' = h (q's vector moved to p's chart, derivative only). RelB p q ↔ Rel q p (the base-point component is automatic, transport_fst), so 'Rel ↔ RelB' is exactly A's Rel.symm, and B's 'RelB is an equivalence' is A's transport_self/Rel.symm/Rel.trans. In B ⇒ A, transport_transport (the chain rule) is derived from transitivity of ∼ in B via the moved tuple (x, ψ, (T(ψ∘φ⁻¹)(φ x,h)).2); transport_mem (Tf maps TO into TO', Prop 2.6(3)) is not implied by B and is re-proved directly from IsScSmoothRetractMap.tangentMap_mapsTo — B presupposes it (it is needed for the moved tuple to be a tuple).
overlap: 196 shared project theorems: retract/tangent infrastructure (retractTangent_eq, proposition_2_4, proposition_2_6_2/_3, retractTangentMap_eqOn, theorem_1_21, IsChart.compatible, TangentPre.vec_mem_image/toBase_vec_fst/mem_retractTangent_image_iff), plus the argument of transport_mem (IsScSmoothRetractMap.tangentMap_mapsTo, retractTangent_fst_mem) which is re-proved verbatim in transport_mem'. The chain-rule proof of transport_transport (retractTangentMap_comp, retractTangentMap_inter_isOpen) is not reused: it comes from B's transitivity.
